item: E1: quadratic-fit coordinates for Lienard half-arcs (143b): model midpoint H(lambda,kappa,r) of the profile lambda*u+kappa*u^2/2 and P,Q,R,S,G; global fit (lambda,kappa,r)->(H,H_r,r) a diffeomorphism onto {|M|<r,|v|<1} (Thm 3.6); transport law P lambda_r+Q kappa_r=0, D kappa=-(R/G)(lambda-k(h)), D lambda-kappa=(S/G)(lambda-k(h)) (Lemma 3.7)
item_type: F5 (change of representation: arc endpoint data (M,M_r) -> fitted model parameters), F1 flavour (new defined objects H,P,Q,R,S,G)
analysis_mode: Text level only. No lake build or comparator run (shared checkout, per orchestrator). Dependency chains computed from data/items/143_lean.json (extract_lean.py v3) by BFS/closure over `uses` edges.
lean_status_why: H,P,Q,R,S,G are defined verbatim (QuadraticCoordinates.lean:20-26), the global fit is formalized in full generality as existence + uniqueness + analyticity of (fitD,fitK) on {r>0,|M|<r,|v|<1} (GlobalFit.lean:82-110) with P,G>0, and the transport law is proved verbatim (ActualFitTransport.lean:105) by the paper's subtract-and-solve argument; the only restriction is that the transport law is instantiated for the quintic profile family rather than a general smooth phi.
lean_gaps: Transport law is stated only for QuinticProfile.profile a (a : Fin 6 -> R), i.e. phi(u)=F(sqrt(2u)) with deg F<=5, at positive base height (hh : 0<h). The paper's Lemma 3.7 is for any phi in C^inf(0,inf). The proof uses only generic lemmas (PositiveTransport.transport_midpoint/transport_v are generic in an analytic parametrized profile Phi), so a general-Phi version is a mechanical refactor (~150 lines), but it is NOT in the release. Same for the shape comparisons (QuinticFit.kappa_width_pos, axisKappa_lower/upper): Fin 6-specific.

Lean requires analytic profiles (ContDiffAt R omega Phi on u>0, plus a local_flow hypothesis); the paper works with C^inf profiles. Irrelevant for polynomial F, relevant for reuse on piecewise or merely smooth F.

Theorem 3.6's 'diffeomorphism' is not packaged as a single Lean object (no OpenPartialHomeomorph / Diffeomorph); it is spread over fit_spec, fit_unique, fitK_analytic, fitD_analytic plus H_abs_lt / Hr_abs_lt. Mathematically equivalent.

Height-zero (axis) fit is a separate layer (AxisFit.lean: axisKappa/axisLambda via QuadraticFit.fitK applied to axis data; joint_limits), matching the paper's Lemma axis-extension + continuity of the inverse.
Comparator is exact for the headline (encard <= 2 and = 2; family.json match_check). Comparator does not mention E1 (test 2 pass).
comparator_chain_notes: Every consecutive pair is a direct `uses` edge in data/items/143_lean.json (checked). Files: Main.lean:20, UpperAssembly.lean:67/42, AxisCases.lean:21, CurvaturePositive.lean:75, ActualFitTransport.lean:55/105, GlobalFit.lean:92, QuadraticCoordinates.lean:20. fit_transport also uses QuadraticCoordinates.transport_H/transport_Hr (QuadraticSlices.lean:82,152) and G_pos.

Shortest chain main -> H (BFS): main -> upper_bound -> upper_nonnegative -> AxisFlow.matching_isolated_case2 -> matchingDelta_zero_bound_of_third -> secant_identity -> axisV_conditional -> axisFit_spec -> QuadraticCoordinates.H.

Case 3 and case 4 also reach H and fitK_spec (matching_zeros_case3 -> matchingDelta_zero_bound -> matchingDelta_crossing -> axisV_conditional -> axisFit_spec -> H; matching_case3_gap -> axisKappa_lower -> joint_limits -> fitK_analytic -> fitK_spec). Case 4 reaches fit_transport via axisLambda_lt -> intercept_height_deriv. Case 1 (no_periodic_case1) and sharpness do not use E1.

Extractor numbers: H has 311 transitive dependents in the 1274-decl DAG (frac 0.317, ~52% of the Secs 3-7 core); fitK_spec 98 (0.10, dominated 0.04); fit_transport 23 (0.024). Dominated shares are ~0 because the target is also reached through case 1 / sharpness branches; knocking out E1 disconnects cases 2-4.

speedup_targets.title: Lins-de Melo-Pugh bound for degree <= 4: at most ONE limit cycle (Li-Llibre 2012 for n=4; LMP 1977 for n=3)
speedup_targets.statement: For every real polynomial F with deg F <= 4, x'=y-F(x), y'=-x has at most one limit cycle. (Li-Llibre also prove hyperbolicity; not part of this target.)
speedup_targets.reference: C. Li, J. Llibre, Uniqueness of limit cycles for Lienard differential equations of degree four, J. Differential Equations 252 (2012) 3142-3162 (21 pp); A. Lins, W. de Melo, C. Pugh, On Lienard's equation, LNM 597 (1977) for n=3.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Li-Llibre 21 journal pages (method not read: full text unreachable); no Lean formalization anywhere (none found).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: NOT a corollary of Theorem 1.1 (which gives only <=2 for deg<=4), but falls out of the family's own case lemmas in a few lines. With a5=0 the reflection F->-F (limitCycle_encard_neg) lets one assume a3>=0 instead of a5>=0, which removes case 2 entirely: a1>=0 gives case 1 (no periodic orbit, or the even/centre case with no isolated zeros), a1<0 gives case 3, where matching_zeros_case3 already bounds ALL zeros of the matching function by 1. Case 3 uses E1 decisively: axisKappa is fitK of the axis data, kappa_range_height/axisKappa_lower bound the fitted curvature by the actual curvature (curvature comparison), and matchingDelta_zero_bound converts kappa_+ > kappa_- at zeros into Delta'>0 via v_kappa = G/P > 0. The proof does NOT use fit_transport or the model inequality (E2): transitive closure of {matching_zeros_case3, no_periodic_case1, limitCycle_encard_le_matching, limitCycle_encard_neg, no_isolated_matching_even} = 827 decls / 7,746 DAG lines (65% of main's 11,947), of which 165 decls / 1,438 lines depend on H; model_inequality and fit_transport are outside it. 143b does not mention that it re-proves Li-Llibre.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: high (21-page paper -> ~40-80 Lean lines of glue given the library). Caveat: this measures the global-fit half of E1 (fit + curvature comparison + crossing lemma), not the transport law; it is near-in-distribution (same system class g=x, lower degree).
speedup_targets.confidence: 0.8 that the glue proof goes through as sketched (text-level check of hypotheses: matching_zeros_case3 needs a1<0, 0<=a3, 0<=a5, satisfied with a5=0; no_periodic_case1 needs some odd coefficient nonzero, else no_isolated_matching_even).
speedup_targets.ablation_design: Arm A: full OAI library. Arm B: library minus AxisCases/UpperAssembly (prover must rebuild case 3 from E1 + kappa_range_height). Arm C: library minus QuadraticCoordinates/GlobalFit/ConditionalFit/AxisFit and dependents (no E1). Speedup = budget(C)/budget(B).

speedup_targets.title: Zhang Zhifen uniqueness theorem, restoring force g(x)=x
speedup_targets.statement: If F is smooth (polynomial for the Lean version), F(0)=0, and F'(x)/x is nondecreasing on (0,inf) and on (-inf,0) (not constant near 0), then x'=y-F(x), y'=-x has at most one limit cycle (hyperbolic if it exists).
speedup_targets.reference: Zhang Zhifen, Acta Math. Sinica 1958 (Chinese); Zhang Zhifen et al., Qualitative Theory of Differential Equations, AMS Transl. Math. Monographs 101 (1992), Ch. 4; Coppel 1989 survey. Exact theorem numbers unverified (search snippet / domain knowledge; full text not read: arxiv.org and ddd.uab.cat unreachable).
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: ~4-8 pages (divergence-integral comparison of two orbits) unverified (search snippet / domain knowledge; full text not read: arxiv.org and ddd.uab.cat unreachable); no Lean formalization found.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: In Filippov coordinates u=x^2/2, phi_+'(u)=F'(x)/x for x>0 and phi_-'(u)=F'(x)/x for x<0 (u decreasing in x), so the hypothesis is exactly phi_+''>=0>=phi_-''. The fitted-curvature range lemma then gives kappa_+(0,r) > kappa_-(0,r) and matchingDelta_zero_bound gives Delta'>0 at every zero: <=1 cycle. This is the paper's case-3 template with the coefficient sign test replaced by the Zhang hypothesis. Needs a strict separation at the axis (paper used delta>0 from p''->inf); with only weak monotonicity a nonconstancy argument is needed.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: med (a few lines on top of E1 + curvature range + matching versus a multi-page divergence argument), but the matching layer for general F is not in Lean
speedup_targets.confidence: 0.6 (the reduction is clean; the boundary/axis strictness needs checking)

top5.target: LMP degree <=4 (<=1 cycle; Li-Llibre 2012, LMP 1977 n=3)
top5.argument: The cleanest measurable speedup: a 21-page known theorem becomes ~40-80 lines of Lean glue over the release library (flip F->-F to make the x^3 coefficient nonnegative, then case 1 or case 3). The decisive step is E1's crossing lemma (matchingDelta_zero_bound: kappa_+>kappa_- at zeros => Delta'>0) and the fitted-curvature range. 143b does not note this consequence. Caveats for grading: it reuses only the global-fit half of E1 (no transport law, no E2), it stays in the same system class, and an ablation (arms B/C) is needed to attribute the speedup to E1 rather than to the matching plumbing.
